title: Savoy cabbage and bean soup with eggs

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a plain whole food or a staple like vegetable stock, tinned beans, cheese and bread, with no jars, stock pots or factory products.

supermarket.reason: Leeks, potatoes, Savoy cabbage, cannellini beans, eggs, vegetarian hard cheese and bread are all everyday Tesco items at ordinary prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a lidded pan and a grater, and cooking eggs in a simmering soup is well within a confident beginner's reach.

works.reason: The amounts are sensible for four: 1.2 litres of stock to 400g potatoes, a tin of beans and half a cabbage gives a hearty broth, and a covered simmer will set the eggs even if the hollows soon close up.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes is fair for slicing two leeks, peeling and cubing the potatoes, shredding the cabbage and grating the cheese, and the 8, 15, 5 and 5 minute stages roughly match the 30 minutes of cooking printed.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item, including the thyme, salt and pepper, is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: A hot cabbage, bean and potato soup suits a cold 2 January lunch, and the Savoy cabbage is a main component rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and in plain British English, with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling lunch with vegetables, beans, eggs and cheese, served with bread, and a family would happily cook it again.
